plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment: gene-level Salmon counts for 12,000 genes across 12 human kidney samples (counts.csv, 12000 x 13 — one gene-id column plus 12 sample columns), with metadata.csv giving one row per sample and a single `condition` factor, 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle controls, unpaired. The research question — which transcription factors drive the treated-vs-control response — is answered by inferring TF activity from a gene-level differential expression statistic against a curated signed TF-target regulon, not by looking at TF transcript levels themselves (TF mRNA is a poor proxy for TF activity, and with n=6 per group individual TF genes will rarely clear FDR).

T1S1 runs the differential expression: PyDESeq2 (Python only, per the user constraint) on the raw Salmon gene-level counts with design ~condition and control as the reference level, producing a full per-gene result table with the Wald statistic retained — the Wald stat is the input the TF-activity step needs, so no shrinkage-only output is acceptable. The profile flags that the record does not state whether a length correction was applied to the Salmon output; the step must check for non-integer values and round rather than fail silently, and report what it found. Independent filtering and low-count filtering are handled inside the step; no batch term exists (single batch) and the design is unpaired, so ~condition is the complete model.

T1S2 takes the signed DE statistic vector and runs TF activity inference with decoupler (installed, v2.2.0) against the human CollecTRI regulon staged in the reference store (source/target/weight, +1 activating / -1 repressing). Univariate linear model (ULM) on the single Wald-statistic contrast is the method decoupler documents for a bulk two-group contrast; a consensus/multi-method cross-check is added as a robustness read. Activity sign gives direction (activated vs repressed in aldosterone-treated), and the regulon size per TF is reported because small regulons give unstable scores. The step must report the fraction of dataset genes that intersect the regulon — with only 12,000 genes present, coverage is the main threat to the result and it has to be stated, not assumed.

T1S3 grounds the top TFs biologically: it checks whether the leading-edge target genes behind each top TF are actually the aldosterone/mineralocorticoid-responsive genes one would expect (SGK1, SCNN1A/B/G, NR3C2, FKBP5, TSC22D3, PER1), and runs pathway enrichment of the DE gene list against the human WikiPathways sets in the reference store. This is the sanity check that separates a real mineralocorticoid signal from regulon-artefact noise. NR3C2/MR itself may or may not be represented in CollecTRI; the step reports its status explicitly rather than assuming it drives the answer.

Power is the honest limitation throughout: 6 vs 6 unpaired detects large coordinated shifts, which is precisely what TF-activity aggregation over regulons is good at, but individual TF calls near the significance boundary should be reported as provisional.
